    Independent statement of Theorems A and B #

    These definitions use only Mathlib. They state the two main theorems of Multiplicative bases and deformations of representation-finite algebras:

    • Theorem A. Every finite-dimensional representation-finite algebra over an algebraically closed field has a normed multiplicative basis.
    • Theorem B. Every basic finite-dimensional representation-finite algebra over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from two is standard.

    Modules are right modules, that is, modules over the opposite algebra. Connections to the proof library are proved in separate modules.

    Representation-finite algebras #

    source
    structure MultiplicativeBasisDeformations.Statement.IndecomposableFamily (k A : Type u) [Field k] [Ring A] [Algebra k A] :
    Type (u + 1)

    One representative of each isomorphism class of finite-dimensional indecomposable right modules. Existence of such a family expresses finite representation type.

    • size : ℕ
    • obj : Fin self.size → ModuleCat Aᵐᵒᵖ
    • finite (i : Fin self.size) : Module.Finite k ↑(self.obj i)
    • indecomposable (i : Fin self.size) : CategoryTheory.Indecomposable (self.obj i)
    • distinct {i j : Fin self.size} : Nonempty (self.obj i ≅ self.obj j) → i = j
    • complete (M : ModuleCat Aᵐᵒᵖ) : Module.Finite k ↑M → CategoryTheory.Indecomposable M → ∃ (i : Fin self.size), Nonempty (M ≅ self.obj i)

            source
            structure MultiplicativeBasisDeformations.Statement.IsNormedMultiplicativeBasis {k A : Type u} [Field k] [Ring A] [Algebra k A] {ι : Type u_1} (b : Module.Basis ι k A) :
            Prop

            A normed multiplicative basis: products of basis elements are zero or basis elements; the basis contains a complete set of primitive orthogonal idempotents; and it meets every radical power (rad A)^n, n ≥ 1, in a basis of that power.

            • multiplicative (i j : ι) : b i * b j = 0 ∨ ∃ (l : ι), b i * b j = b l
            • idempotents : ∃ (E : Finset ι), (CompleteOrthogonalIdempotents fun (i : ↥E) => b ↑i) ∧ ∀ i ∈ E, IsPrimitiveIdempotent (b i)
            • radicalPow (n : ℕ) : 1 ≤ n → Submodule.span k (⇑b '' {i : ι | b i ∈ Statement.radicalPow k A n}) = Statement.radicalPow k A n

                  Basic algebras #

                  source
                  def MultiplicativeBasisDeformations.Statement.IsBasic (A : Type u) [Ring A] :
                  Prop

                  A is basic: it has a complete set of primitive orthogonal idempotents e_i whose principal right ideals e_i A are pairwise nonisomorphic. Here e_i A ≅ e_j A is expressed by elements x ∈ e_i A e_j, y ∈ e_j A e_i with xy = e_i and yx = e_j.
